title: Temperature
examples: Teacher, what is the difference between degrees Celsius and degrees Fahrenheit?
How do I read a thermometer that goes below zero?
Can you show me an example of a negative temperature?

explain.say: Today we learn about measuring temperature using degrees. We use two main scales for this. One is Celsius, and the other is Fahrenheit.
The Celsius scale is very common for science. Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius. This is a key point to remember.
The Fahrenheit scale is sometimes used in other places. Water freezes at thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit. Remember this difference.
Sometimes temperatures are below zero. When we go below zero, we use a minus sign. This shows a negative number.
If the temperature is minus four degrees Celsius, we write it as negative four. This means it is below zero.

faq.q: What is the difference between Celsius and Fahrenheit?
faq.a: Celsius is often used in science and many countries. Fahrenheit is used in some other places. They measure the same thing but use different numbers.
asks: Which scale is better to use?
Do I always use one or the other?

faq.q: How do I read a thermometer that goes below zero?
faq.a: You look for the minus sign, or negative sign. If the line is below zero, you use the minus sign in your answer.
asks: What does a minus sign mean for temperature?

faq.q: Is minus four degrees Celsius really cold?
faq.a: Yes, minus four degrees Celsius is quite cold. It is four degrees below the freezing point of water.
asks: How cold is negative four degrees?
What is below zero on a thermometer?

faq.q: Do I need to know both scales?
faq.a: It is good to know both scales for general knowledge. However, you only need to use the scale your teacher asks for.
asks: Which scale should I focus on?

faq.q: What is the freezing point of water in both scales?
faq.a: In Celsius, water freezes at zero degrees. In Fahrenheit, water freezes at thirty-two degrees.
asks: Where is zero on the thermometer?
What is the water freezing point?

facts: The Celsius scale is widely used in science.
Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius.
Water freezes at thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit.
A negative temperature means it is below zero degrees.

quiz.say: If the temperature is minus two degrees Celsius, what symbol do you use?
quiz.why: The minus sign shows the temperature is below zero degrees Celsius.

wrong.0: This is wrong because it means the temperature is exactly at freezing point.
wrong.2: This is wrong because it shows the temperature is two degrees above zero.
wrong.3: This is wrong because it is a completely different temperature measurement.

quiz.say: Which temperature scale uses thirty-two degrees for freezing water?
quiz.show: Which scale uses 32° for freezing water?
quiz.why: The Fahrenheit scale uses thirty-two degrees for water to freeze.

wrong.1: Celsius uses zero degrees for water to freeze, not thirty-two.
wrong.2: Kelvin is another scale, but we are only learning Celsius and Fahrenheit now.
wrong.3: Degrees is a unit, not the name of the scale itself.
